content.title: No. 1 Duke escapes No. 5 St. John's 80-75 to advance to the NCAA tournament Elite 8
content.text: Dylan Darling couldn’t be the hero for St. John’s for a second straight game.Days after hitting a buzzer-beater to give the Red Storm a second-round win over Kansas, Darling’s game-tying 3-point attempt with less than five seconds to go bounced off the rim as No. 1 Duke advanced to the Elite Eight with an 80-75 win over No. 5 St. John’s.The Red Storm still had a chance to get the game to overtime in the waning seconds thanks to Duke’s struggles at the free throw line. Isaiah Evans starred for Duke, but he made just one of two free throws before Darling’s 3-point attempt. And Cameron Boozer missed the front end of a 1-and-1 with 32 seconds to go.AdvertisementBut Boozer iced the game with two seconds to go by making two free throws after a St. John’s foul tore the front of his jersey.The Blue Devils will play either No. 2 UConn for a spot in the Final Four on Sunday.Caleb Foster returns in ‘special performance’Evans’ trip to the free-throw line in the waning seconds was his first of the game. He led all scorers with 25 points as he was 10-of-15 from the field and had four of Duke’s five made 3-point attempts.But Duke was also powered by the return of point guard Caleb Foster, who played for the first time since fracturing his right foot in the Blue Devils’ regular-season finale against North Carolina.“He had no business playing today,” Duke coach Jon Scheyer told CBS. “He was determined, that was one of the most special performances I’ve ever seen.”AdvertisementScheyer said those words after a long, emotional pause. Foster’s impact was clear on him. And especially during the second half.After going scoreless in the first half, Foster scored 11 points in the second half and made a driving layup with less than 90 seconds to go that put the Blue Devils up by five.Foster played 18 minutes in his first action in three weeks and also added three rebounds and two assists. After starting the entire season, Foster came off the bench on Friday night and entered the game with Patrick Ngongba II after the first TV timeout.Ngongba played 17 minutes in his second game back from injury. Ngongba missed that North Carolina game and the entire ACC tournament with a sore right foot, but returned in the second round against TCU.AdvertisementSt. John’s was hot from behind the arcThe Red Storm do not rely on the 3-point shot. St. John’s entered the game shooting just 33% from behind the 3-point line.But they’ve been a different team in the NCAA tournament. St. John’s made 10 3-pointers against Northern Iowa in the first round, and then 11 against Kansas in that second-round win. It was just the third and fourth times all season that St. John’s had made at least 10 3-point field goals in a single game.Friday night, St. John’s had 10 made 3-pointers in the first half. It’s why the Red Storm had a one-point halftime lead.And in the second half, St. John’s was 12-of-25 from behind the arc at one point. But as the game went on, the Johnnies cooled off.AdvertisementSt. John’s made just one of its last seven 3-point attempts to finish 13-of-32. It was still a performance well above the team’s season average. But one that also needed another make or two for the upset bid to become reality.Zuby Ejiofor had 17 points and grabbed 8 rebounds while dishing out 6 assists to lead St. John’s. Sophomore forward Ruben Prey — who wasn’t on the court much in the second half — scored 12 points as he made all four of his 3-point attempts.
